subject: Trading
title: The Roaring Twenties and 1929
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Roaring Twenties and 1929 usable.

hook.text: The 1920s were electric: jazz, automobiles, radio—and a stock market that seemed to only go up. Then came Black Tuesday.

buildup.text: From 1921 to 1929, the Dow Jones rose over 500%. Ordinary Americans bought stocks on margin for the first time.

discovery.text: On October 29, 1929—Black Tuesday—16 million shares traded as prices collapsed. Billions evaporated in hours.

twist.text: The crash was just the beginning. The Dow wouldn't recover its 1929 peak until 1954—twenty-five years later.

climax.text: The 1929 crash triggered the Great Depression, reshaping banking, regulation, and the entire financial system.

punchline.text: The longest party ended with the longest hangover.

quiz.question: How long did it take the Dow to recover its 1929 peak?
